text:
Izzy (PMM): heads-up  we need a compact, probe-resistant battlecard and two short launch blurbs for next week's webinar. Focus: clear differentiators vs cloud managed endpoints and infra vendors + inbound routing for benchmark requests.
Rohan (Growth): we should A/B two headline styles: benefit-forward and tradeoff-forward. Ads vs nurture segmentation.
Elena (Field): reps want three ultra-short lines (latency, cost, migration) and a 6-line objection cheat sheet. Keep it copy-paste friendly.
Sam (Bench): topline benchmark notes (gated deck has details): p95 ~125ms at sustained 1k RPS in our harness; batching + KV cache yielded ~3x token efficiency on multi-turn chat; fallback policies preserved throughput during a forced node eviction test.
Noor (Content): public phrasing must be "customer-observed"; internal battlecard can show exact numbers and a single anonymized prompt comparison slide.
Harper (Sales Ops): routing rules idea: if lead.company_size >= 600 OR lead.budget_est >= 150k => AE; if clicked benchmark_slide => tag bench_warm and create AE task. Also decide whether to promote any attendee who watches >50% to AE for a test cohort.
Izzy (PMM): proposed public-safe lines:
- "Customer-observed p95 ~125ms under sustained load"
- "Measured token savings (up to ~3x) with batching + prefix caching"
- "One API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments"
Elena (Field): internal 1-liners (copy-ready):
- Latency: "Ask for benchmark deck  slide: p95 ~125ms under sustained load"
- Cost: "Customers see ~2-4x token efficiency on chat after batching and light quantization"
- Migration: "Same API surface  prompts port, not infra rewrite"
Noor (Content): objection drafts (6 short items):
1) "Why not just use cloud endpoints?" -> "Cloud endpoints are easy to start but don't provide deterministic routing, tail protection, or KV caching. Redwood gives production controls and predictable economics."
2) "Is model ownership sufficient?" -> "Model choice matters, but serving/runtime determines latency and cost at scale. We optimize kernels, batching, and caching across environments."
3) "What about latency spikes during incidents?" -> "We provide routing fallbacks and capacity tiers to limit tail spikes and maintain SLAs."
4) "How much effort to migrate?" -> "Most customers port prompts with the same API; migration is configuration and prompt tuning, not infra rewrite."
5) "Can we keep keys on-prem/KMS?" -> "Yes  we support customer-managed keys and private control planes for regulated workloads."
6) "What's the real cost delta?" -> "Benchmarks vary by workload; request the gated deck for per-model, per-sequence results."
Rohan (Growth): headline variants:
A) "Stabilize LLM latency and lower per-token spend"
B) "Why managed endpoints often fail tail-latency tests"
Decision: run A in paid ads, B in nurture emails. Tag ad clicks with opener=A.
Sam (Bench): deliverables: 2-slide benchmark summary + appendix with harness notes and anonymized example prompt (due 4310003300).
Noor (Content): deliverables: 1) public blog-safe paragraph (customer-observed language) 2) 1-page internal battlecard with 6 rebuttals and 3 demo soundbites (due 4310003450).
Harper (Sales Ops): deliverables: implement SFDC routing rule, bench_warm tag, and AE task automation (due 4310003550). Create test cohort for >50% watchers.
asset-bot: s3://redwood-assets/webinar-431000/bench-summary.pdf uploaded at 4310003255
Izzy (PMM): final decision: Ads=A, Emails=B, field gets internal lines + "ask for benchmark deck" CTA. Public materials use "customer-observed" phrasing. Check-ins every 8h in this thread. Move fast. :rocket:
